title: Well-ordered sets: least elements, induction, and recursion

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 29–31 (section 6, especially Lemma 6.2 and Theorem 6.6), notes updated January 31, 2026

summary: Study well-orders and their initial segments, prove induction from least counterexamples, and construct unique recursive functions from rules on earlier histories.
abstract: Put one new point after all the natural numbers. The resulting order still has a first element in every nonempty subset, but the new point has no immediate predecessor. Such examples show how induction and recursive definitions can continue beyond finite stages. Induction works on any well-order: a property holds everywhere if, at each point, its truth at all earlier points implies its truth there. Likewise, a rule specifying a value from the previously assigned values determines a unique function, provided it gives exactly one output for every possible earlier assignment.
